hook: Paying one hundred dollars a month on five thousand of card debt?

blocks.narration: Paying one hundred dollars a month on five thousand of card debt? It may honestly never get paid off at all.
blocks.visual: A clay figure runs on a treadmill made of a credit card, going nowhere, glossy blue light

blocks.narration: Here is why. At twenty-four percent a year, the interest on five thousand dollars is about one hundred dollars every month.
blocks.visual: A meter beside the treadmill shows a monthly interest drip pouring back onto the card

blocks.narration: So a one hundred dollar payment covers the interest and almost nothing else. The balance just sits there, month after month.
blocks.visual: Coins go into a slot and immediately pour back out the other side, the balance pile unchanged

blocks.narration: Bump the payment to one hundred fifty dollars and it takes about fifty-six months, with around thirty-three hundred dollars in interest.
blocks.visual: The treadmill finally creeps forward, a long road ahead stretching to a distant finish flag

blocks.narration: At two hundred fifty dollars a month, it is gone in about twenty-six months, with roughly fourteen hundred fifty dollars in interest.
blocks.visual: The road shortens dramatically, the finish flag now close and bright

blocks.narration: Every extra dollar above the interest goes straight to the balance. That is why small increases make such a big difference.
blocks.visual: Extra coins land directly on the debt pile, which shrinks with each one

blocks.narration: Your statement must show how long minimum payments take. Card issuers are required to print that warning, and it is usually shocking.
blocks.visual: A magnifying glass slides over a paper statement, revealing a small boxed warning

blocks.narration: Pay more than the minimum whenever you can. Share this with someone carrying a balance. It might save them thousands.
blocks.visual: The clay figure steps off the treadmill and crosses the finish line, confetti falling

cta: Share this with someone carrying a balance. It might save them thousands.

captions.hook_line: Paying $100 a month on $5,000 of credit card debt? It may never end 😳
captions.body: At 24% APR, $5,000 accrues about $100 of interest a month, so a $100 payment barely moves the balance. At $150 a month it takes about 56 months and roughly $3,300 in interest; at $250, about 26 months and $1,450.

youtube_title: Why $100 a Month Never Pays Off $5,000
